Card payment (scheme rails): Physical card or card credential; may be tokenized
UPI payment (India): UPI ID/VPA, QR, intent, or collect flow, depending on app
Wallet-enabled card payment: Wallet UI presents a tokenized card credential in supported implementations
Operational note / caveat: Wallet can be an interface/credential container, not necessarily a separate rail

UPI payment (India): UPI app, merchant QR, intent, or collect request
Operational note / caveat: Availability and exact flow vary by region, device, provider, and merchant setup

Card payment (scheme rails): Cardholder, merchant, acquirer/processor, card network, issuer
UPI payment (India): Payer app/PSP bank, NPCI UPI network, remitter bank, beneficiary/payee bank, merchant
Wallet-enabled card payment: Cardholder, wallet/token service, merchant/PSP, acquirer/processor, card network, issuer
Operational note / caveat: The precise participant set depends on online vs in-person payment and product architecture

Card payment (scheme rails): Issuer approves or declines through network routing
UPI payment (India): Payer authorization (UPI PIN or supported method); banks and UPI network process the request
Wallet-enabled card payment: Underlying card authorization typically goes through card network to issuer using tokenized credential
Operational note / caveat: Do not equate wallet authentication with final issuer authorization

Card payment (scheme rails): Card authorization is followed by clearing and settlement; timing and merchant payout depend on arrangements
UPI payment (India): UPI is designed for real-time account-to-account transfer; merchant pool/account credit and reconciliation follow the bank/provider arrangement
Wallet-enabled card payment: Uses the underlying card payment rails for card-funded purchases; merchant payout follows acquirer/provider arrangements
Operational note / caveat: Avoid promising a universal settlement time without the actual contract and payment type

Card payment (scheme rails): Card security controls; network/device tokenization may be used
UPI payment (India): UPI PIN and participating bank/app controls; do not collect/store PIN
Wallet-enabled card payment: Token replaces the primary card number in supported tokenized flows; cryptogram/device context may be used
Operational note / caveat: Never handle plaintext PIN, OTP, full PAN, or CVV in operational tracker

Card payment (scheme rails): Authorization reversal/void and post-capture refund are distinct; disputes/chargebacks are separate
UPI payment (India): Failed debit may trigger reversal under the scheme rules; completed transfer generally cannot be stopped by payer; complaint routes depend on status
Wallet-enabled card payment: Refund usually returns through underlying card flow; tokenization does not make refund a separate rail
Operational note / caveat: Use transaction ID and status query before retrying an unknown outcome

Card payment (scheme rails): Authorization rate, issuer declines, timeouts, capture gaps, settlement reconciliation, chargebacks
UPI payment (India): Technical vs business declines, pending/deemed-approved states, debit reversal, beneficiary credit, merchant confirmation
Wallet-enabled card payment: Token provisioning, device/token failures, authorization, device support, underlying-card refund status
Operational note / caveat: Segment metrics by channel, provider, issuer/acquirer, country, and response code when available
